definition: Based on a random choice or a whim rather than on a reason.
example: The rule seemed arbitrary because nobody could explain why it existed.

options.text: Decided after studying all the facts
Decided by whim rather than by reason
Decided by a vote of the whole class
Decided long ago and rarely changed

explanation: Arbitrary means decided by whim rather than by reason. Great job!

definition: Kind and generous, wanting to do good for others.
example: The benevolent neighbor shoveled snow from every driveway on the street.

options.text: Strict and careful about the rules
Wealthy and proud of being rich
Clever and quick to find mistakes
Kind and eager to help others

explanation: Benevolent means kind and eager to help others. Nice work!

definition: The quality of being short and to the point.
example: The speech was praised for its brevity; it said everything in two minutes.

options.text: The state of being very long
The quality of being short and clear
The courage needed to face a hard challenge
The skill of speaking in public

explanation: Brevity is the quality of being short and clear. Well done!

definition: Something that causes or speeds up a change or an event.
example: The new teacher was the catalyst for starting a robotics club at school.

options.text: Something that prevents any change
Something that sets off a change
A tool used to measure change
A record of changes over time

explanation: A catalyst is something that sets off a change. You got it!

definition: Complete and covering everything that is needed.
example: The guidebook is comprehensive, with maps, history and tips for every trail.

options.text: Short and covering only one part
Easy to understand and clearly written
Complete and covering all the parts
Arranged from newest to oldest

explanation: Comprehensive means complete and covering all the parts. Great job!

definition: A feeling or idea that a word suggests beyond its exact meaning.
example: The word home has a warm connotation of comfort and family.

options.text: The exact meaning that is given in a dictionary
A feeling a word suggests beyond its meaning
The way a word is spelled
The sound a word makes when spoken

explanation: A connotation is a feeling a word suggests beyond its exact meaning. Nice work!

definition: To think about something carefully and for a long time.
example: I sat by the window to contemplate which book to choose for my report.

options.text: To decide something in a split second
To forget about something right away
To write about something in a diary
To think about something for a long time

explanation: To contemplate is to think about something for a long time. Well done!

definition: Believable and able to be trusted.
example: The scientist's report was credible because it came with clear evidence.

options.text: Hard to believe and likely false
Believable and worth trusting
Admired and praised by many people
Ready to lend money to other people

explanation: Credible means believable and worth trusting. You got it!

definition: To become worse over time.
example: The old wooden fence will deteriorate if it is never painted.

options.text: To slowly become better with age
To stay the same for many years
To slowly become worse in quality
To be replaced by something much newer

explanation: To deteriorate is to slowly become worse in quality. Great job!

definition: Careful and hard-working in doing a task.
example: The diligent student checked her answers twice before handing in the test.

options.text: Quick and able to finish before others
Calm and willing to wait
Clever and good at guessing
Careful and steady in doing work

explanation: Diligent means careful and steady in doing work. Nice work!

definition: A difference between things that should match.
example: The teacher noticed a discrepancy between the two lists of names.

options.text: A difference between things that should match
A close match between two lists
A total or sum of two amounts
A list of the items in a set

explanation: A discrepancy is a difference between things that should match. Well done!

definition: To spread out in different directions.
example: Pigeons disperse when a bicycle rolls through the square.

options.text: To gather together in one place
To spread out in different directions
To move in a straight line
To circle around a single spot

explanation: To disperse is to spread out in different directions. You got it!

definition: Unusual or odd in behavior, but in a harmless way.
example: My eccentric uncle wears a bright hat every day, even in summer.

options.text: Ordinary in every way
Central and in the middle
Unusual in a harmless way
Excited and full of energy

explanation: Eccentric means unusual in a harmless way. Great job!

definition: The ability to understand and share another person's feelings.
example: She showed empathy by sitting with her friend after the bad news.

options.text: A strong wish to win every argument
The habit of keeping your feelings private
A talent for guessing what comes next
The ability to share another person's feelings

explanation: Empathy is the ability to share another person's feelings. Nice work!

definition: Fair and equal to everyone.
example: The coach made an equitable plan so that every player got time on the field.

options.text: Fair only to people you know
Decided by the loudest voice
Fair and equal to everyone
Planned to help only a few

explanation: Equitable means fair and equal to everyone. Well done!

definition: Unpredictable and not following a regular pattern.
example: The weather was erratic all week, sunny one hour and stormy the next.

options.text: Steady and the same every day
Careful and thought out well in advance
Gentle and calm from start to end
Unpredictable and without a pattern

explanation: Erratic means unpredictable and without a pattern. You got it!

definition: To be a clear example of something.
example: Her kindness to every new student helps to exemplify the school's values.

options.text: To be a clear example of something
To copy the style of something
To explain the reasons for something
To list all the rules of something

explanation: To exemplify is to be a clear example of something. Great job!

definition: Careful about spending money; not wasteful.
example: Because we are frugal, we pack lunches instead of buying them each day.

options.text: Quick to spend money on every sale
Skilled at earning large sums
Careful about how money is spent
Happy to share money with a friend

explanation: Frugal means careful about how money is spent. Nice work!

definition: Enjoying the company of other people; sociable.
example: The gregarious puppy ran up to greet every person in the park.

options.text: Grateful and quick to say thanks
Gentle and quiet around animals
Friendly and fond of company
Great at telling long stories

explanation: Gregarious means friendly and fond of company. Well done!

definition: A system that ranks people or things from highest to lowest.
example: The chart showed the hierarchy of the company, from the manager down to the new interns.

options.text: A system that ranks things by level
A group of friends who work together
A list of names in alphabetical order
A map that shows where things are

explanation: A hierarchy is a system that ranks things by level. You got it!

definition: Based on facts rather than on personal feelings or opinions.
example: A good judge stays objective and looks only at the facts.

options.text: Based on feelings and opinions
Based on facts rather than feelings
Based on a friend's advice
Based on rules from long ago

explanation: Objective means based on facts rather than feelings. Great job!

definition: Hard to find, catch or remember.
example: The elusive fox slipped away before we could get a clear photo.

options.text: Easy to spot from far away
Hard to find, catch or hold on to
Famous and known by everyone
Tame and used to being near people

explanation: Elusive means hard to find, catch or hold on to. Nice work!

definition: Naturally and permanently a part of something.
example: Some risk is inherent in every sport, so players wear protective gear.

options.text: Added later by someone else
Passed down from parents to their children
Easy to take away and replace
Part of something by its very nature

explanation: Inherent means part of something by its very nature. Well done!

definition: A new idea, method or device.
example: The folding bicycle was a clever innovation for people who live in small apartments.

options.text: An old tradition kept alive
A repair made to a broken tool
A lesson taught by an expert
A new idea, method or device

explanation: An innovation is a new idea, method or device. You got it!

definition: Following what is right and fair; morally good.
example: It is ethical to return a wallet you find, even when no one is watching.

options.text: Right and fair in what you do
Popular and liked by most people
Fair only when it helps you win
Clever and good at winning

explanation: Ethical means right and fair in what you do. Great job!

definition: To place two things side by side to show how they differ.
example: The artist chose to juxtapose a bright red door against a gray wall.

options.text: To stack many things in a pile
To remove one thing from a pair
To set two things side by side
To pose a question to two people

explanation: To juxtapose is to set two things side by side. Nice work!

definition: Clear and easy to understand.
example: Her lucid explanation made the tricky math problem feel simple.

options.text: Lucky and likely to succeed
Bright and glowing in the dark
Clear and easy to understand
Long and full of hard words

explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand. Well done!

definition: Extremely careful about small details.
example: He was meticulous about his model, checking each tiny piece before gluing it.

options.text: Extremely careful about details
Extremely quick at finishing work
Very fond of making rules
Ready to try anything once

explanation: Meticulous means extremely careful about details. You got it!

definition: Ordinary and a bit dull; part of everyday life.
example: Washing dishes is a mundane chore, but someone has to do it.

options.text: Lively and out of the ordinary
Rare and worth a lot of money
Odd and hard to explain to others
Ordinary and part of daily life

explanation: Mundane means ordinary and part of daily life. Great job!

definition: A warm, sometimes sad longing for happy times in the past.
example: Looking at old photos filled him with nostalgia for his childhood summers.

options.text: A longing for happy times in the past
A plan for happy times to come
A habit of forgetting all the old things
A collection of old photos

explanation: Nostalgia is a longing for happy times in the past. Nice work!

definition: A very small difference in meaning, color or feeling.
example: A good translator notices every nuance in the way a sentence is said.

options.text: A very small difference in meaning
A big change in a story
A mistake in how a long word is spelled
A rule that decides a meaning

explanation: A nuance is a very small difference in meaning. Well done!

definition: Not aware of what is happening around you.
example: She was so focused on her book that she was oblivious to the loud music.

options.text: Alert and watching every detail
Bothered by every little sound
Forgetful of things from the past
Unaware of what is going on around you

explanation: Oblivious means unaware of what is going on around you. You got it!

definition: A statement or situation that seems to contradict itself but may still be true.
example: It is a paradox that the more you share your knowledge, the more you have.

options.text: A guess that turns out to be right
A statement that seems to contradict itself
A question with only one answer
A rule that has no exceptions

explanation: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself. Great job!

definition: Dealing with things in a practical, sensible way.
example: Her pragmatic solution was to carry an umbrella instead of hoping for sun.

options.text: Dreamy and focused on imagined things
Practical and focused on what works
Playful and focused on having fun
Strict and focused on old rules

explanation: Pragmatic means practical and focused on what works. Nice work!

definition: To keep putting off a task until later.
example: If you procrastinate, the homework will pile up before the weekend.

options.text: To keep putting a task off until later
To finish a task before it is due
To rush through a task carelessly
To share a task with a partner

explanation: To procrastinate is to keep putting a task off until later. Well done!

definition: Wise and careful in thinking ahead.
example: It was prudent to check the weather before we planned the trip.

options.text: Wise and careful about the future
Proud and sure of every choice
Polite and kind to every guest
Pleased with whatever happens

explanation: Prudent means wise and careful about the future. You got it!

definition: The art of using words well to speak or write in a convincing way.
example: The student used strong rhetoric to persuade the class to recycle.

options.text: The habit of speaking very softly
A list of hard words and their meanings
The art of using words to persuade
A style of writing in rhyme

explanation: Rhetoric is the art of using words to persuade. Great job!

definition: Happening now and then, not regularly.
example: We had sporadic showers all afternoon, but none lasted long.

options.text: Happening now and then
Happening every single day
Happening only at night
Happening in a steady rhythm

explanation: Sporadic means happening now and then. Nice work!

definition: To support a claim with proof or evidence.
example: You must substantiate your answer with a quote from the story.

options.text: To repeat a claim more loudly
To back up a claim with proof
To doubt a claim without reason
To copy a claim from a book

explanation: To substantiate is to back up a claim with proof. Well done!

definition: Only on the surface; not deep or thorough.
example: A superficial look at the test did not show the tricky questions.

options.text: Better than all the others
Large and covering a wide area of land
Only on the surface and not deep
Deep and based on careful study

explanation: Superficial means only on the surface and not deep. You got it!

definition: Holding on firmly and not giving up.
example: The tenacious climber kept trying until she reached the top.

options.text: Tender and gentle with others
Thankful and quick to give thanks
Talkative and always chatting
Firm and unwilling to give up

explanation: Tenacious means firm and unwilling to give up. Great job!

definition: Calm, quiet and peaceful.
example: The lake was tranquil in the early morning, without a ripple on the water.

options.text: Busy, loud and crowded
Calm, quiet and peaceful
Cold, dark and windy all day long
Wide, flat and empty

explanation: Tranquil means calm, quiet and peaceful. Nice work!

definition: Found everywhere at the same time.
example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous, and you can see them in every public place.

options.text: Found in every place at once
Found in only one place
Found only in very old places
Found mostly in the morning

explanation: Ubiquitous means found in every place at once. Well done!

definition: Using more words than necessary.
example: His verbose answer took ten minutes when a single sentence would have done.

options.text: Short, with only a few words
Poetic, with lines that rhyme
Wordy, with more words than needed
Silent, with no sound at all

explanation: Verbose means wordy, with more words than needed. You got it!

definition: Playful and fanciful in an unusual way.
example: The whimsical drawing showed a teapot with tiny legs, walking down a hill.

options.text: Serious and based on hard facts
Gloomy and full of gray colors
Playful and imaginative in an odd way
Plain and meant for daily use

explanation: Whimsical means playful and imaginative in an odd way. Great job!

definition: Lacking seriousness; focused on small, unimportant things.
example: She felt that buying a tenth pair of sunglasses was a frivolous way to spend her savings.

options.text: Unimportant and lacking serious purpose
Important and filled with purpose
Free and open to anyone who wants to join
Fussy about tiny details

explanation: Frivolous means unimportant and lacking serious purpose. Nice work!

definition: Lasting for only a very short time.
example: A soap bubble is ephemeral; it pops within seconds.

options.text: Permanent and hard to erase
Large and filling the whole sky
Ancient and found in old books
Short-lived and quickly gone

explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived and quickly gone. Well done!

definition: Able to recover quickly after trouble or a setback.
example: The resilient team lost the first game but came back to win the finals.

options.text: Able to stay away from trouble
Able to predict when trouble will start
Able to cause trouble for others
Able to bounce back after trouble

explanation: Resilient means able to bounce back after trouble. You got it!

definition: Able to be used in many different ways.
example: A plain white shirt is versatile because it goes with almost anything.

options.text: Useful in many different ways
Useful only for one task
Valuable because it is old
Easy to store in a small space

explanation: Versatile means useful in many different ways. Great job!

definition: Little known or hard to understand; unclear.
example: The author's obscure poems are loved by only a few readers.

options.text: Famous and known to everyone
Little known and hard to understand
Clear and very easy for anyone to follow
Large and printed in bold

explanation: Obscure means little known and hard to understand. Nice work!
